title: cProfile for performance profiling

overview.what:
cProfile is a built-in Python tool that measures exactly how long each function in your code takes to run.

Imagine taking a long road trip that took 10 hours instead of 5. You look at your GPS history to see exactly where you spent the most time (3 hours at a restaurant, 2 hours in traffic). cProfile is the GPS history for your code. It shows you which functions are the slow 'traffic jams'.

```python
import cProfile

def slow_task():
    # A loop that does a lot of work
    total = 0
    for i in range(1000000):
        total += i
    return total

# This runs the function and prints a speed report
# cProfile.run('slow_task()')
```

The rule is: **never guess what makes your code slow; use cProfile to measure it.** It gives you a report showing the number of times a function was called (`ncalls`) and the total time spent inside it (`tottime`).
overview.why: It prevents you from wasting hours optimizing the wrong part of your code. You find the exact bottleneck instantly.

why_learning_this: You will know exactly which 5 lines of code are making your entire application slow.
You will sound professional when you say, 'I profiled the code and found the bottleneck'.

common_mistakes.title: Guessing instead of measuring
common_mistakes.explanation: You assume a database query is slow and spend days fixing it, when cProfile would have shown you the real delay was a slow `for` loop.

common_mistakes.title: Ignoring the call count
common_mistakes.explanation: A function might be very fast, but if `ncalls` shows it was called 1 million times, it becomes the bottleneck.

recall_questions.q: Explain what cProfile does in your own words, as if to a classmate.
recall_questions.answer: It measures how long your code takes to run, breaking down the time spent in each individual function.

recall_questions.q: Why is it important to look at the 'ncalls' column in a cProfile report?
recall_questions.answer: Because a function might be fast on its own, but calling it thousands of times can make the whole program slow.

understanding_checks.question: You profile your code. Function A takes 0.001 seconds per call but is called 10,000 times. Function B takes 2.0 seconds but is called once. Which one takes more total time?
understanding_checks.answer: Function A takes 10 seconds total (0.001 * 10,000). Function B takes 2 seconds. Function A is the real bottleneck.
understanding_checks.why: Never guess what makes your code slow; use cProfile to measure it. The total time spent in a function is what actually slows down your app.

understanding_checks.question: A teammate says, 'My code is slow, so I will rewrite every single function to make it faster.' What is a better approach?
understanding_checks.answer: Use cProfile to find the one or two slowest functions, and only rewrite those.
understanding_checks.why: Most of the execution time is usually spent in a very small portion of the code. Profiling prevents you from wasting time optimizing fast code.

code_walkthrough.focus: print('cProfile would show slow() taking 99% of the time.')

aha_moment.prediction: If a function is extremely simple and fast, can it ever be the main bottleneck in a cProfile report?
aha_moment.why: Yes, if it is called millions of times in a loop. `ncalls` matters just as much as `tottime`.
